newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Youthful minister says Russia needs young leaders.
newsitem.headline: Youthful minister says Russia needs young leaders.

text.p: Boris Nemtsov, a first deputy prime minister at the age of 37, said on Tuesday Russia needed young leaders to take it into the next century.

"Russia must go into the 21st century only with young people, including in its leadership," Itar-Tass news agency quoted Nemtsov as telling students to loud applause during a tour of the Siberian city of Krasnoyarsk.
Nemtsov, a former provincial governor who is widely regarded as a potential presidential candidate, said young leaders were needed in industry to help push through economic reforms.
"The younger the leadership of an enterprise, the more effective its economy is," he said.
Nemtsov made no reference to Yeltsin, 66, or Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, 59, who brought him into the cabinet last month alongside 41-year-old first deputy prime minister Anatoly Chubais.
Nemtsov has praised Yeltsin regularly and refers to him as a kind tsar in a new book.
